newsitem.title: USA: Fujitsu says holder suit "without merit".
newsitem.headline: Fujitsu says holder suit "without merit".

text.p: Fujitsu Ltd said Thursday allegations raised in a shareholder suit seeking to stop its offer to acquire shares it still does not own in computer maker Amdahl Corp are without merit.

In a statement read on the phone by a spokeswoman, the Japanese computer conglomerate said: "While we haven't seen a copy of the lawsuit, the allegations contained in the press release issued by the plaintiff's lawyers are without merit."

Earlier today, the law firm of Milberg Weiss Berhad Hynes & Lerach LLP said that the complaint alleges that Fujitsu's $12 a share offer, or about $850 million for the Amdahl shares it still did not own, is "unfair and grossly inadequate."

The complaint alleges that the intrinsic value of Amdahl's common stock is "materially in excess of the amount offered, giving due consideration to the company's growth and anticipated operating results, net asset value and profitability," the law firm said. The lawsuit seeks to recover damages on behalf of public shareholders of Amdahl.
Fujitsu, which already owns a 42 percent stake in Amdahl, announced its proposal to acquire the rest of the U.S. computer maker on Wednesday.
